column1: # P2-G6 NAMED FAULT MATRIX.
# Machine-readable form of the plan's required record:
#   branch -> fault -> fast target -> resource oracle -> mutation.
# The driver reads columns 1-3 (name, fault-summary, get-ordinal); columns 4-6
# document the uncovered upstream error branch each fault reaches, the oracle
# that judges it, and the mutation that proves the row is non-vacuous. Add a row
# by editing this file, the backend script (arm the fault on the same ordinal)
# and, if a new mutation is wanted, mutate.sh -- the driver's plan-count is this
# file's row count, so a drift between table and driver reds the scenario.
# get-ordinal is (driver WARMUP=8) + row index -- the driver issues 8 clean
# warmup gets first, so the faults sit at ordinals 9..14 and the driver asserts
# each row's ordinal equals the get it is about to issue (a table/backend/driver
# drift reds the scenario, never passes on an unfaulted get).
# name
